main_mystery: Who is actually controlling what Calder observes — and will Lena's strategy survive the settlement without Calder overriding her plan?
truth: Lena detected Calder's surveillance in Chapter Three. From that point she controlled portions of what he could see — repeated routines, red receipts, door seals, a paper planner, and a certified honeytoken. She designed the evidence trap that forced Grant to commit to a false chain of custody at the settlement. Calder believed he was the watcher; he was the watched. The decisive sequence of visible events was directed by Lena, not Calder or Grant.

red_herrings.description: Lena's visible forgetfulness and paranoia in Chapters 1-2 appear to be genuine deterioration. The reader (and Calder) are led to believe Grant may be telling the truth about her instability.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as manufactured by Grant's manipulation and Lena's controlled visibility.

red_herrings.description: Lena's repeated routines appear to be compulsion or stress behavior. Calder interprets them as evidence of deterioration.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as diagnostic tests: each routine was designed to test what reaches Grant and what Calder records.

red_herrings.description: Lena's direct looks toward Calder's window appear unconscious or flirtatious. Calder believes she is unaware and attracted.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as deliberate detection: she identified the reflected status light and message timing.

red_herrings.description: The envelope Lena mails in Chapter Eight appears to be a genuine packing checklist and key-return plan. Grant believes it proves she intends to abandon the property.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as a certified honeytoken containing false information and a unique phrase designed to expose mail interception.

red_herrings.description: Calder's refusal to enter Lena's apartment before Chapter Eleven appears to be professional caution. Grant reads it as continued reliability.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as Calder's decision to preserve independent evidence after witnessing Grant's recorded entry.

major_reveals.description: Lena detects the surveillance. She identifies Calder's reflected camera status light and connects it to Grant's message timing.
major_reveals.note: Partial reveal — Lena knows she is watched but not Calder's identity, loyalty, or recording method.

major_reveals.description: Grant's recorded entry. Calder's unedited camera captures Grant using a master credential to enter Lena's apartment during a deleted interval.
major_reveals.note: Calder learns Grant manufactures evidence. Calder begins keeping independent originals.

major_reveals.description: The certified honeytoken is mailed. Lena mails a false checklist and unique phrase to herself.
major_reveals.note: Lena begins the evidence trap. Grant does not yet know the envelope's contents are false.

major_reveals.description: Lena confronts Calder. She knows his surname, his role, and that he keeps originals. She tests his archive policy.
major_reveals.note: Surveillance alliance begins. Calder changes allegiance under explicit limits set by Lena.

major_reveals.description: Grant repeats the unique phrase 'Friday key return.' This proves mail interception without requiring video evidence.
major_reveals.note: Value One of the honeytoken pays off. Lena learns Grant intercepted the envelope.

major_reveals.description: Mae prints the local credential audit. Independent physical evidence survives digital deletion.
major_reveals.note: The audit corroborates Grant's pattern of unauthorized entry and footage deletion.

major_reveals.description: Full control reveal. Lena explains the planner, red receipts, door seals, and honeytoken strategy. Calder learns he was watched, predicted, and directed.
major_reveals.note: The central mystery is resolved. The decisive sequence of visible events was controlled by Lena.

major_reveals.description: Evidence transfer. Calder transfers one encrypted duplicate of the original surveillance archive to Detective Cross.
major_reveals.note: Evidence no longer depends on Calder's loyalty or survival.

major_reveals.description: False chain exposure. Grant authenticates the envelope and asserts a false chain of custody. Calder's unedited footage contradicts him.
major_reveals.note: The climax. Grant loses because he commits to a calculated lie that contradicts independent evidence.

major_reveals.description: Lena chooses Calder without dependencies. She asks him to return without recording equipment after the settlement.
major_reveals.note: The romance payoff. Lena chooses Calder only after she no longer needs him as a witness.

clues.description: Reflected camera status light in Calder's window. Lena notices a small red glow that appears only when she is in the courtyard during specific hours.
clues.note: First clue that Lena detects surveillance. The light is visible only from her courtyard position.

clues.description: Message timing correlation. Grant messages Lena about something she just noticed within minutes of her courtyard appearance.
clues.note: Lena connects the message timing to the camera light. She infers Grant is receiving reports.

clues.description: Calder's unedited camera records Grant entering Lena's apartment with a master credential during a deleted interval.
clues.note: Calder learns Grant manufactures evidence. The footage is the first independent proof of unauthorized entry.

clues.description: Calder's field notebook timestamp of the entry. Handwritten record independent of digital deletion.
clues.note: Corroborates the unedited footage. Establishes a physical record of Grant's entry.

clues.description: Certified envelope with false checklist and unique phrase 'Friday key return.' Lena mails it to herself, clips the lower-right corner, and records tracking.
clues.note: The honeytoken. Value One (information leak) pays off in Ch12. Value Two (physical corroboration) pays off in Ch17.

clues.description: Lena learns Calder's surname from a lobby package label addressed to 'Reed.'
clues.note: Lena identifies Calder by name before the confrontation.

clues.description: Lena infers Grant hired Calder from the timing of the surveillance start relative to the settlement date.
clues.note: Lena confirms Calder's role as Grant's operative before confronting him.

clues.description: Grant tells Calder to watch for a 'Friday key return.' The exact phrase from the sealed envelope.
clues.note: Value One of the honeytoken. Proves mail interception without video evidence.

clues.description: Lena's planner entry recording the unique phrase and tracking number. Establishes the phrase was in the envelope before Grant repeated it.
clues.note: Corroborates the honeytoken chain. Lena's physical record proves the phrase was sealed.

clues.description: Mae prints the local credential audit from the board terminal. Shows Grant's master credential was used during deleted intervals.
clues.note: Independent physical evidence that survives digital deletion. Corroborates the broader pattern.

clues.description: Lena's paper planner with timestamps, red-receipt placements, and door-seal checks. Cannot be remotely altered.
clues.note: Lena's primary record of her controlled visibility. Revealed to Calder in Ch14.

clues.description: Folded red receipts placed beside disturbed objects. Build a physical timeline of Grant's entries.
clues.note: Lena's method of tracking environmental disturbances. Each receipt marks a confirmed entry.

clues.description: Clear doorframe seals. Lena places them before her morning walks and checks them upon return.
clues.note: Detects unauthorized entry during her absence. Each broken seal is a confirmed entry.

clues.description: Lena's repeated routines are revealed as diagnostic tests, not compulsion. Each test was designed to map what reaches Grant and what Calder records.
clues.note: The central reframe. Calder learns the visible behavior was controlled, not symptomatic.

clues.description: Calder transfers one encrypted duplicate of the original surveillance archive to Detective Cross. The evidence index is also delivered.
clues.note: Evidence no longer depends on Calder's loyalty or survival. Cross now holds an independent copy.

clues.description: Grant formally authenticates the envelope, clipped corner, checklist, and unique phrase at the settlement. He asserts a false recycling-area custody chain.
clues.note: Grant commits to a calculated lie. He does NOT state he took the envelope.

clues.description: Calder's unedited lobby footage shows Grant removing the same clipped envelope from Lena's mailbox.
clues.note: Contradicts Grant's false chain of custody. The footage establishes Grant stole the envelope.

clues.description: Postal tracking record for the certified envelope. Shows delivery to Lena's mailbox, not the recycling area.
clues.note: Corroborates the footage. The envelope was delivered to Lena's mailbox, not discarded.

clues.description: Calder's field notebook with timestamps of Grant's entry and envelope removal.
clues.note: Handwritten record independent of digital deletion. Corroborates the footage.

clues.description: The surveillance contract with Grant's instructions. Establishes Grant hired Calder to document instability.
clues.note: Establishes Grant's motive and method. Shows the scope of Calder's assignment.

clues.description: Mae's printed credential audit. Shows Grant's master credential was used during the intervals when footage was deleted.
clues.note: Corroborates the broader pattern of unauthorized entry and footage deletion.

clues.description: Lena asks Calder to return without recording equipment. She grants no unrestricted access and chooses when he enters, when he watches, and when the curtain closes.
clues.note: The romance payoff. Lena chooses Calder only after all dependencies end.
